# RICD-Tell

> The first empirical test of Recursive Information-Container Dynamics (RICD), a theory of system health built to apply across domains and tested one domain at a time. Tell is the instrument: a pre-registered distress tracker for U.S. higher education built from public federal data (IPEDS, College Scorecard).

## What RICD is
- A formal model with defined quantities, in docs/ (the RICD 17.7 Spine, the core engine, and the Catalog, an optional reference for edge cases and specialized trackers).
- Divergence between an institution's official, operational and meta layers (Spine Definition 6.2, section 6.3.3); resource debt (section 7.9); coverage, break-even and the drift-type or shock-type slide (section 10.3a); anchors that move the point of no return (Definitions 10.3a.7 and 10.3a.8).
- Not statistical risk modeling and not a "grand theory": its quantities are defined before any test, and it makes claims about a domain only after an adapter for that domain is built and tested.

## What Tell has shown
- Tracker v3 passed its pre-registered test on 987 held-out institutions (closures 2019 to 2025): 32 of 56 closures caught, J 0.49.
- It beat every baseline: flagging every for-profit (J 0.31), critical slowing down (J -0.02), and, at its committed flag cut points, a size-and-sector model (J 0.49 against 0.38; public and nonprofit 0.29 against 0.09; both difference intervals above zero).
- It catches edge cases the size-and-sector proxy misses (9 closures against 1) and its anchor sensor cleared 14 flags on supported colleges, none of which closed.
- It measures the anchors and the strain they carry across the sector, and finds that most closures are slow drifts, not sudden shocks.
- In law schools, which report outcomes directly, schools in the bottom tenth on bar passage or employment collapsed ten times as often.

## How to read it
- Size and sector are the anchoring itself in higher education (large and public institutions are anchored and do not close), so they are a ceiling on overall ranking, not a bar the theory failed to clear.
- Tell's accuracy comes from the theory's quantities working together (divergence, resource debt, coverage, drift, anchors); the data readings chosen for each layer are proxy selection under pre-registered tests.
- The meta channel (abnormal staff exit with governance voice) is built and pre-registered for the blind retest against the 2026-27 IPEDS release (July 2027).
- Every protocol was committed before outcomes were looked up; the full record of earlier versions is in reports/Model evolution.md.
